subject: AcmeCloud: data-path boundaries and fallback choreography for inference service
messages:
From: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@acmecloud.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: 2026-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Data-path boundaries & fallback choreography - Redwood inference

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the RFP response packet — we've got a few follow-ups from our security and platform teams. Two specific asks to help us complete the Security Architecture Questionnaire: 

1) Can you provide a clear demarcation between the control plane and data plane for Redwood's hosted inference? Our reviewers want to see what network boundaries exist, how identity/elevation is handled between planes, and whether there's any shared runtime that could allow cross-tenant lateral movement.

2) In the event of a zone or node failure, what is the fallback choreography for in-flight requests? Specifically: where does traffic re-route, how is KV/cache provenance preserved (if at all), and what egress/egress-filtering guarantees do you maintain during and after failover?

If possible, please attach a diagram that shows the data-path (client -> edge -> inference runtime -> model store/KV -> external services) with the ACLs/firewall boundaries annotated. Also let us know if you can provide a short (1–2 page) summary we can forward to our auditors.

We're targeting a security review completion by next Friday (2026-09-03). Would you be able to deliver the artifacts and a 30-minute walkthrough by then?

Appreciate it — Alicia
Alicia Ramos
Sr. Security Engineer, AcmeCloud
security@acmecloud.com

- acme-questionnaire-sect-4.pdf (original RFP section)

Subject: Re: Data-path boundaries & fallback choreography - Redwood inference

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear asks. We're happy to provide the artifacts and a short narrative for your auditors. High-level notes up front:

- Control plane is separated into a customer-managed control VPC (for Private) or a logically separated control cluster in our hosted control plane; the runtime (data path) runs in isolated tenant pools with per-tenant KV cache and egress controls.
- During zone/node failures we fail open to a lower-capacity remote pool (same region or cross-region per customer preference) with enforced egress policy and a cold-warm cache rebuild.

I'm attaching a first-draft annotated diagram (redwood-inference-dataflow-diagram-v1.pdf) and an example mapping template (acme-mapping-template.xlsx) that shows ACLs and subnet demarcations. Jordan will lead the diagram updates; Ben will pull the cache provenance/log excerpt.

We can deliver a 30-minute walkthrough — are you available 2026-09-01 10:00 PT or 2026-09-02 09:00 PT?

I'll follow up with an internal plan and timeline.

Best,

Jordan / Ben — forwarding Alicia's ask. Short plan and owners below; please reply with ETA for your artifacts so I can confirm with Acme: 

- Jordan: Update the dataflow diagram to show explicit control-plane endpoints, management plane VPCs, and per-tenant runtime pools. Add arrows for auth token flow and management-plane-only egress (no customer data). Estimated work: 3–4 hours.
- Ben: Provide a 1-page cache provenance excerpt (example logs showing KV write/evict sequence, and TTL semantics) plus a short paragraph describing how we rebuild/rehydrate caches post-failover. Also include any sidecar proxy rules that enforce tenant isolation at runtime. Estimate: 2–3 hours.
- Marissa (me): Draft the 1–2 page auditor narrative (control plane vs data plane boundary, failover choreography, egress guarantees) and consolidate artifacts. Will pull in ops runbook snippet for failover sequence.

Key constraints: for hosted customers we prefer same-region fallback but can enable cross-region for higher resilience per contract. Make sure the diagram annotates where traffic is encrypted in transit and where HSM/KMS keys are used for model artifacts.

Reply-all with ETAs by end of day and I'll lock a walkthrough time with Acme.

Hi Alicia — thanks for waiting. Please find below the deliverables and a concise summary suitable for your auditors; the annotated diagram and mapping template are attached. If you'd like the raw log excerpts for deeper review we can provide an encrypted bundle under NDA.

Deliverables (attached / linked):
- redwood-inference-dataflow-diagram-v1.pdf — annotated flow showing: edge ingress (TLS-terminated at per-region edge), control-plane management endpoints (separate VPCs; management API authenticated via mTLS), tenant runtime pools (isolated namespaces + sidecar proxy per-tenant), model store access (KMS-wrapped artifacts), and egress filter boundaries.
- acme-mapping-template.xlsx — ACL/subnet mapping and recommended CIDR lists for allow/block rules.
- Auditor summary (below) — 2 pages included in the PDF.

Short auditor summary (2‑minute read):
- Control plane vs data plane: The control plane (management APIs, orchestration, billing) is logically separated from the data plane (request ingress, inference runtime, KV cache) and enforces strict RBAC and mTLS for all management operations. No customer inference payloads traverse the control-plane network.
- Isolation model: Tenant isolation is achieved via a combination of network namespaces, per-tenant sidecar proxies, and per-tenant KV namespaces. Sidecars enforce request-level tenant tokens and mTLS to the runtime. Model artifacts are stored encrypted with KMS and mounted read-only.
- Fallback choreography: For transient node/zone failures, in-flight requests are re-routed to a warm standby pool within the same region when available; if capacity constraints require, requests are routed to a pre-approved cross-region pool. During failover we preserve request ordering where possible; KV caches are rehydrated via a deterministic warm-start process and provenance markers (write sequence ids) are used to avoid duplication.
- Egress & proof guarantees: All egress is subject to per-customer allowlists and network ACLs. During failover egress filtering remains enforced; we actively monitor and log all egress attempts and provide audit traces.

Proposed next step: a 30-minute technical walkthrough to step through the diagram and runbook. Available slots: 2026-09-01 10:00 PT or 2026-09-02 09:00 PT. Which works for your reviewers?

Best regards,
